title: The internal commutative group functor of a discrete integer representation
statement: Let $G$ be a topological group, $w$ a universe, and $\mathcal R$ the category of discrete continuous integer representations [def-exc-discrete-modules-category]. Give $\mathcal C=\mathrm{DiscreteContAction}(\mathrm{Type}(w),G)$ a Cartesian monoidal structure and braiding. Define $H:\mathcal R\to\mathrm{CommGrp}(\mathcal C)$ as follows. The underlying action of $H(M)$ is the action of $M$ with discrete topology. For $X\in\mathcal C$, equivariant functions $X\to M$ form an additive subgroup of all functions, under pointwise operations. This group-valued presheaf is represented by the underlying action of $M$. Transport its operations through representability to give the internal commutative group law. An equivariant integer-linear map induces the same underlying function, preserving these internal operations. This defines $H$ without postponed data or existence choices.
